drills.name: Form shooting
drills.desc: Slow, close-range makes that groove the shot's skeleton: feet set, ball on the fingertips, elbow under the ball, one-hand release with a full follow-through. Power comes up from the legs through one connected motion — the arm just steers. Perfect reps from three feet beat lazy reps from the arc.
mistakes: Ball resting in the palm instead of on the finger pads.
Elbow flared out so the ball starts and finishes off line.
Snapping the wrist without legs — the shot becomes all arm.

drills.name: Catch and shoot
drills.desc: Feet ready before the ball arrives — hopping or stepping into the catch so the shot releases in one rhythm. The pass's energy flows straight into the lift; any pause to gather is time a closeout uses. Hands present a target early and the eyes find the rim before the catch.
mistakes: Catching flat-footed, then starting the shot from zero.
Drifting sideways on the hop instead of loading straight up.
Eyes on the ball through the catch rather than already on the rim.

drills.name: Pull-up jumper
drills.alt: Stopping off the dribble to shoot
drills.desc: Sprinting into a two-step stop and rising straight up for the shot before the defender can react. The skill is deceleration: the last dribble is snatched up as the feet chop into a balanced one-two stop, hips sinking to absorb the momentum. A vertical rise, not a drift, keeps the shooting pocket identical every time.
mistakes: Floating forward on the release so every shot has a different depth.
Stopping tall with straight legs — no balance, no lift, sore knees.
Telegraphing the pull-up by slowing the dribble two beats early.

drills.name: Layups (both hands)
drills.desc: The right-hand and left-hand layup off the correct footwork — outside foot, inside foot, up — using the backboard's square as the target. The knee on the shooting side drives up to convert run into rise, and the ball stays high and protected. Weak-hand competence doubles your angles at the rim.
mistakes: Taking off from the wrong foot so the body drifts under the rim.
Laying the ball flat at the rim instead of high off the square.
Slowing down on the gather because the footwork isn't automatic yet.

drills.name: Floater
drills.alt: Soft high runner over the big man
drills.desc: A one-handed touch shot lofted off the run before the shot-blocker can reach it. It launches off either foot from just inside the free-throw line, with a stiff wrist pushing the ball high and dead — spin and arc do the work, not power. Balance through the gather is what makes the touch repeatable.
mistakes: Shooting it flat like a jumper — the floater lives on high arc.
Leaning into the defender's body instead of rising off a balanced plant.
Only practicing off the dominant foot and hand.

drills.name: Euro step
drills.desc: After the gather, the first step attacks one side of the defender and the second steps long past their opposite hip. It weaponizes the two legal steps as a full change of direction, and the ball swings low and away from the swipe. Each step is a genuine lateral push — long, low and committed.
mistakes: Two short choppy steps in the same line — no defender is moved.
Carrying the ball high through the gap where hands are waiting.
Gathering too early and running out of steps before the rim.

drills.name: Stationary pound dribbling
drills.alt: Hard two-ball and one-ball dribble reps
drills.desc: Dribbling as hard as the floor allows — waist-high pounds, low pounds, crossovers in place, with one ball then two. Hard dribbles return the ball faster, which is where handle speed actually comes from. The stance stays athletic: knees bent, chest up, eyes anywhere but the ball.
mistakes: Soft, polite dribbles that give defenders a full second per bounce.
Standing tall and watching the ball instead of dribbling by feel.

drills.name: Crossover
drills.alt: Snapping the ball across to change direction
drills.desc: A hard, low dribble across the body paired with a shoulder-and-foot fake that sends the defender the wrong way. The ball travels below the knees on a sharp V, and the outside foot pushes off explosively into the new lane. The sell — head, eyes and a real weight shift — matters more than the dribble itself.
mistakes: Crossing high and slow through the steal zone at the defender's hands.
No weight shift on the fake — the dribble changes sides but nobody moves.
Standing upright through the move instead of staying in the hips.

drills.name: Combo moves (behind-back, between-legs)
drills.alt: Chaining dribble moves at game speed
drills.desc: Linking crossover, between-the-legs and behind-the-back into two- and three-move chains that answer a live defender. Each move must flow out of the previous one's footwork with no reset dribble between. The chain is only as good as the burst that exits it — every combo ends with an attack, not another move.
mistakes: Dribbling combos for their own sake with no exit burst attached.
Moves rehearsed only at cone speed collapse against real hands.
Behind-the-back thrown wide, forcing a chase-down of your own dribble.

drills.name: Defensive slides
drills.alt: Lateral shuffle in a low stance
drills.desc: The lateral shuffle that keeps a defender's chest in front of the ball: wide base, hips below the ball-handler's, steps that push off the trail leg without the feet ever clicking together. Endurance in this stance is a strength quality — the first player to stand up loses the possession.
mistakes: Clicking the heels together mid-slide, surrendering the base.
Crossing the feet to recover instead of opening the hips and running.
Reaching with the hands while the feet stop moving.

drills.name: Closeouts
drills.alt: Sprinting to a shooter under control
drills.desc: Sprinting at a catching shooter, then chopping the feet into short stutter steps to arrive balanced — high hand at the shot, hips ready for the drive. The art is trading the last two sprint steps for control so a pump fake doesn't send you flying. Angle the approach to take away the shooter's strong side.
mistakes: Sprinting all the way in and flying past the pump fake.
Closing out flat-footed and upright, beaten by the first dribble either way.
Both hands down, conceding an uncontested rhythm three.

drills.name: Box-outs
drills.alt: Sealing your man off the boards
drills.desc: At the shot, find a body first: hit, pivot into their path, sit into a wide low seal with forearms up, then go get the ball. The contact is a leg-driven hip press — a standing squat against a moving opponent. Rebounds are won on the floor before anyone jumps.
mistakes: Watching the ball's flight instead of hitting a body first.
Boxing out tall and narrow — easy to spin off or push under the rim.
Holding the seal forever and never releasing to attack the ball.

drills.name: Lateral quickness work
drills.desc: Short lateral shuffles, mirror drills and reactive cone touches that build side-to-side speed on command. Quickness here is hip strength plus short ground contacts — the glute medius and adductors fire like pistons while the feet stay under the hips. It underwrites every defensive possession.
mistakes: Long, bounding side steps that leave the base wide open mid-air.
Rising out of the athletic stance as fatigue sets in.

drills.name: First-step explosiveness
drills.alt: Winning the first yard off the dribble
drills.desc: The blow-by step: a violent 45-degree push off the back leg, chest low over the lead knee, ball and foot arriving together. It is a sprinter's block start disguised as a basketball move — horizontal force wins the first yard, and the first yard wins the drive. Train it loaded, then rehearse it with the ball.
mistakes: First step lands under the body instead of out past the defender's foot.
Standing tall at launch — the chest must project over the lead knee.
Ball pushed out lazily behind the step, begging for a poke-away.

drills.name: Vertical jump training
drills.alt: Jumping higher off one and two feet
drills.desc: Building the two-foot bounce and the one-foot running jump behind blocks, boards and finishing at the rim. Height comes from force into the floor: heavy triple-extension strength plus fast plyometric contacts that teach the tendons to return it. The arm swing alone is worth inches when it is timed with the hips.
mistakes: Only jumping — without a strength base, plyos have nothing to return.
Cutting the countermovement short instead of sinking into the hips.
Landing stiff-legged rep after rep and donating the gains to the knees.
